ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: An 8-bit ADC converts analog voltage in the range of 0 to +5 V to the corresponding digital code as per the conversion characteristics shown in the figure. For \(V_{\text{in}} = 1.9922\,\text{V}\), what is the digital output in hex?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a staircase curve of an ADC conversion characteristic, with the vertical axis labeled “Digital Output in Hex”; the low-end codes can be seen in order as 00H, 01H, 02H, 03H. The horizontal axis is the analog input, labeled Vin in mV / Analog Input. Near the horizontal axis, tick marks such as 0, 9.8, 19.6, 39.2, 58.8 mV are marked. The interval between adjacent code centers of the staircase is about 19.6 mV, consistent with the 8-bit ADC quantization step size over the 0 to 5 V range. Reasoning: An 8-bit ADC has a total of 2^8 = 256 codes, and the full-scale range is 5 V, so 1 LSB = 5/256 = 0.01953125 V. Given Vin = 1.9922 V, the ideal decimal code value is Vin / LSB = 1.9922 / 0.01953125 ≈ 102.0006. According to the staircase characteristic shown in the figure, the corresponding integer code is taken as 102. Convert 102 to hexadecimal: 102 = 6×16 + 6, therefore the digital output is 66H.
